name: Streetlight Manifesto
label: Victory
lede: Tomas Kalnoky quit Catch 22 after one album, then spent fifteen years re-recording it, touring in a van that kept getting robbed, and fighting Victory Records until he bought his masters back.

eras.title: Quit after one album
eras.text: Kalnoky, born in Prague and raised in East Brunswick, New Jersey, sang on Catch 22's first record and left before the band toured it. Keasbey Nights became a third-wave ska touchstone, and he spent years trying to take it back.

years.h: Catch 22 starts in East Brunswick, New Jersey, with Kalnoky out front
years.p: Tomas Kalnoky, born in Prague, is a teenager when he takes the guitar and the microphone for [[Catch 22|e59b17a9-2c0d-4284-854e-6d51a448091d]], a ska-punk band.

years.h: Keasbey Nights puts Catch 22 on the third-wave map
years.p: Kalnoky writes and sings it, Jamie Egan plays horns, and Victory Records puts it out.

years.h: Kalnoky leaves before Catch 22 tours the record
years.p: He goes back to school. Wikipedia says his parents pushed him toward it; his own page says he went to study visual art.

years.h: Bandits of the Acoustic Revolution record A Call to Arms
years.p: Kalnoky's acoustic project cuts the EP, with early versions of songs he'd rework for Streetlight.

years.h: Ex-Catch 22 players fill out Kalnoky's new band in New Brunswick
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto's four-song demo includes Point/Counterpoint and We Are the Few.
years.xp: The demo line-up: Josh Ansley (bass), Jamie Egan (trombone, trumpet), Tomas Kalnoky (guitar, vocals), Stuart Karmatz (drums), Dan Ross (saxophones) and Pete Sibilia (tenor sax). Paul Lowndes replaced Karmatz and Jim Conti replaced Sibilia; before the first shows Mike Soprano joined on trombone and Chris Thatcher took over drums.

eras.title: Robbed twice in a month
eras.text: The first album came out on the same label as Keasbey Nights, and the first headline show sold out. Then the horn line kept turning over, and thieves hit the band in Jacksonville and again in Paris.

years.h: Everything Goes Numb lands on Victory, Catch 22's label
years.p: Kalnoky's new band debuts on the same label that put out Keasbey Nights.

years.h: Streetlight and Catch 22 trade veiled shots on record
years.p: Streetlight's debut and Catch 22's Dinosaur Sounds both arrive in 2003, and Wikipedia describes each as containing supposed veiled attacks on the other. The bands later made up; Catch 22's Kevin Gunther now books Streetlight's tours.

years.h: Rutgers sells out Streetlight's first headline show
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto headlines for the first time at Rutgers University in New Brunswick, and every ticket goes.

years.h: Bassist Josh Ansley leaves to act
years.p: Ansley quits Streetlight Manifesto to pursue an acting career.

years.h: Jamie Egan out, trumpeter Delano Bonner in at Rowan three days later
years.p: Egan quits before the Ska Is Dead 2 tour. Bonner plays his first show January 25 at Rowan University in Glassboro, New Jersey.

years.h: Streetlight gets to Europe anyway
years.p: The April tour goes ahead despite complications with visas.

years.h: Dan Ross leaves mid-tour for a family crisis; Mike Brown steps in at Baltimore
years.p: Ross later teaches math at Piscataway High School. Brown plays his first US show in Baltimore on May 31.

years.h: Thieves empty the van in Jacksonville
years.p: Roughly $80,000 in instruments and merchandise is gone, and four shows are cancelled.
years.xp: A month later, in November 2005, the band was robbed again in Paris and lost its 24-track hard drive recorder.

eras.title: Keasbey Nights, again
eras.text: Victory planned to reissue Keasbey Nights as it was, so Kalnoky re-made it with Streetlight on the band's own money. The next record of originals reached No. 2 on Heatseekers, and a covers series stopped at one volume.

q: I've always thought it sounded like pure garbage sound-wise.
years.h: Kalnoky remakes Keasbey Nights rather than let Victory reissue it
years.p: Victory planned to reissue the 1998 Catch 22 album unchanged, so Kalnoky re-recorded it with Streetlight on the band's own money. Victory released the remake in March 2006.
years.xp:
Kalnoky said he didn't want fans duped into buying a new edition of something they already had. The new version has new verses, new arrangements, and a text-to-speech interview in place of the original ending of the final track.

AllMusic gave both versions four stars but said the remake lost some of the original's raw, youthful energy.

years.h: Matt Stewart takes the trumpet chair from Delano Bonner
years.p: Bonner leaves Streetlight Manifesto between December 2006 and July 2007, and Stewart steps in.

years.cap: Streetlight Manifesto at Roseland Ballroom, New York, July 19, 2007
years.h: Somewhere in the Between goes on sale at a show four days early
years.p: It reaches No. 2 on Heatseekers and No. 19 on Punknews' list of the year.
years.xp:
The band sold physical copies at a concert four days before the November 13, 2007 release. It reached No. 154 on the Billboard 200 and No. 18 on the Independent Albums chart.

Punknews ranked it No. 19 of the year's 20 best releases; AllMusic gave it 3.5 stars and PopMatters 7 out of 10.

years.h: Jim Conti lands in the hospital with a facial infection
years.p: Streetlight plays shorter sets heavy on older songs while the saxophonist recovers.

years.h: Kalnoky breaks his arm on Warped Tour and keeps singing
years.p: Another guitarist covers his parts while he does.

years.h: 99 Songs of Revolution: Vol. 1 stays the only volume
years.p: Streetlight planned its covers project as a series. As of 2026, volume one is the only one released.

eras.title: Victory, a boycott and a lawsuit
eras.text: The Hands That Thieve was Streetlight's last album for Victory. The fight over it ran through a boycott call, a leak and a lawsuit, and ended with the band buying its own masters.

years.h: A November 6 date for The Hands That Thieve slips twice
years.p: Announced August 22 for November 6, 2012, the album gets pushed to January 2013 by label conflicts and rewrites, then to April 30.

years.src: Wikipedia: Streetlight Manifesto · Wikipedia: Victory Records
years.h: Streetlight asks fans to boycott Victory, Amazon included
years.p: The band says Victory withheld copies of The Hands That Thieve from both the band and its pre-order customers.
years.xp:
Streetlight kept taking pre-orders on its own site with no physical copies to send, and asked fans to skip Victory merch everywhere.

Wikipedia's Victory Records page dates the boycott call to February 2012; the band page says February 2013, which fits the album delays.

years.h: Streetlight says it will stop touring year-round
years.p: After 2013 the band plans to self-release future albums too, and plays out the year on the End of the Beginning Tour.

years.h: Kalnoky's acoustic The Hand That Thieves leaks on its release day
years.p: As Toh Kay, Kalnoky had the acoustic version cancelled after Victory got it removed from Amazon. The leaked files carry that metadata title.

years.h: The Hands That Thieve comes out eleven days after leaking
years.p: Streetlight's last Victory album reaches No. 95 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: It leaked April 19, 2013 and came out April 30. It also reached No. 21 on the Independent Albums chart and No. 19 on Top Alternative Albums.

years.h: Pre-order fans get a blank CD-R and an orange tabby
years.p: The long-delayed package for The Hands That Thieve pre-orders is a digipak with a blank CD-R, a 24-page booklet, and a photo of an orange tabby cat on the cover.

q: @victoryrecords hasn't paid us a cent in royalties in over 2 yrs.
years.src: Wikipedia: Streetlight Manifesto · Wikipedia: Victory Records
years.h: Victory Records sues Kalnoky
years.p: Victory says Streetlight owes it albums, arguing a covers album and a record traded for a $10,000 emergency advance don't count. The band puts the suit at $5 million, not $1 million.
years.xp: Victory's suit also alleged copyright infringement over The Hands That Thieve and the Toh Kay version. Early coverage reported $1,000,000; three days later the band said it was five million.

years.h: Streetlight settles with Victory and buys back its masters
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto and Victory announce the band is leaving the label, and the band buys all of its master recordings for an undisclosed sum.

eras.title: The sixth album, still pending
eras.text: Streetlight announced a sixth album in 2021 and has been circling it since, a loss of trumpeter Matt Stewart in between.

years.h: A sixth album is promised for 2022
years.p: Streetlight Manifesto announces it on July 27, 2021. By early 2023 the band says progress is slow.

years.h: A new song, Mayday, debuts at the Starland Ballroom
years.p: On The Calm Before The Chaos Tour, Streetlight teases it in Sayreville, New Jersey.

years.h: Matt Stewart, trumpeter since 2007, dies at 41
years.p: Stewart died September 10, 2023. Mike Soprano returned for San Francisco and Los Angeles, then Joshua Gawel of Lucky Chops took over.

years.cap: Streetlight Manifesto at the Wiltern, Los Angeles
yt: The Place Behind the Stars teaser
years.h: The Place Behind the Stars gets a June 24 date
years.p: A teaser on April 3 comes first, then the April 9 announcement of the sixth album.

years.h: Eight days before release, The Place Behind the Stars is pulled
years.p: Streetlight postpones indefinitely, then posts three songs to YouTube as pre-release mixes on June 24.
